claims.text: Vector databases function by storing and retrieving data embeddings within a vector space.
Unlike traditional databases that rely on exact matches, vector databases typically use approximate nearest neighbor algorithms to facilitate semantic searches.
Vector embeddings represent data as mathematical points in a high-dimensional space, where each dimension reflects a specific data feature.
The number of dimensions in a vector embedding can vary from a few hundred to tens of thousands based on the complexity of the underlying data.
Various data types, including audio, images, and text, can be converted into vectors.
Machine learning methods like deep learning networks or word embeddings are used to generate feature vectors where semantically related items are positioned near each other.
Vector retrieval workflows can incorporate lexical search or metadata filtering to provide hybrid or filtered results.
Commonly used techniques for similarity search in high-dimensional spaces include inverted files, product quantization, locality-sensitive hashing, and Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs.
Recent performance benchmarks indicate that HNSW-based implementations are frequently among the top performers.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) often uses a vector database to store document embeddings, allowing large language models to retrieve relevant context for specific user prompts.
A vector database is defined as a database system that stores information as high-dimensional vectors representing specific features or attributes.
